summary: STIG-style idle timeouts can log you out during installs, backups and restores that run an hour or more; the usual culprit is `systemd-logind` `StopIdleSessionSec`. If it's non-zero, set `StopIdleSessionSec=7200` in `/etc/systemd/logind.conf`, run `systemctl restart systemd-logind`, then log out and back in.
questions: AAP installer session gets logged out after 15 minutes
How do I increase StopIdleSessionSec for the AAP install?
Backup interrupted by idle session timeout
STIG session timeout breaks AAP installation

answer_card.title: Stop idle logout during installs
answer_card.answer_md:
As root on the installation host:
```ini
# /etc/systemd/logind.conf
StopIdleSessionSec=7200
```
```bash
systemctl restart systemd-logind
```
Log out completely and back in so the session picks it up. `0` already means no timeout.
